response.rationale: All options are unmatched. Ranking is based on clinical closeness to the vignette's description of necrotizing skin lesions. Necrotizing fasciitis and necrotizing cellulitis are both severe necrotizing infections, with fasciitis typically being deeper. Septic emboli can cause skin necrosis but is a mechanism rather than a primary diagnosis of the skin lesion itself. Pressure necrosis is less likely given the description of progression and lack of device use on the ears.
